messages:
ashu: hey @support — customer (acme-inc) escalated: they moved from Free -> Standard yesterday and are now getting bursts of 429s this morning. they say their client unchanged; traffic spiked roughly x10 for a short period. attaching samples they sent.

clare: can you paste one raw response (headers + body) and the approximate time window? also which plan/commit did they purchase (monthly vs annual)?

ashu: pasted one sample below. upgrade from Free -> Standard (monthly) at 2026-03-12T21:08Z. 429s observed between 2026-03-13T08:05:00Z and 2026-03-13T08:18:00Z. response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:07:22 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1773389842
X-Request-Id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
```
body:
```
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Token bucket exceeded for org ID o-ccf9","retry_after":12}
```

max: tagging eng-sre. initial read: looks like token-bucket refill semantics — a short concurrent burst likely went well above per-minute/burst allocation. billing propagation can cause edge cases around plan change, but that usually stabilizes quickly. need full request histogram to confirm client behavior.

nisha: we can approve a one-time temporary burst for up to 6 hours while billing settles, but we need customer approval and a short justification. ping me after support validates this is not an SDK/loop bug.

ashu: customer said they ran a concurrent embedding job plus background retriever tests at the same time. their client snippet:
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":"test payload"}' &
done; wait
```
so ~200 concurrent starts over ~20s; they expected our burst window to absorb that.

clare: that pattern often trips burst protections. concurrent fan-out creates many new connections and consumes request tokens quickly. recommended guidance:
- throttle concurrency (recommend 30–40 for Standard tier)
- add exponential backoff + full-jitter for 429 responses
- batch embeddings to reduce request count (our embeddings endpoint accepts arrays)
- use our official SDK (py/js) which has built-in retry/backoff; raw curl won't handle retries for you automatically

max: artifacts we need before approval/escalation:
- org id
- sample X-Request-Id(s) from 429 responses
- server-side log windows around the timestamps (we'll map API keys to logs)
- a small histogram/timestamps of client request start times + concurrency (even a CSV)

ashu: customer supplied org o-ccf9 and two request ids: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d, rwd-req-0a1b2c3e. asking them to run a short trace (curl --trace-ascii or add a timestamp header) and return the per-request start times.

support-bot: Incident automated note — rate-limit-alert for org o-ccf9 triggered at 2026-03-13T08:06:58Z. AlertID: RL-20260313-229.

max: checked internal metering and config sync logs. plan change was recorded at 2026-03-12T21:08Z; billing state transitioned at 21:09:12Z; policy index updated at 21:09:45Z. routing caches had stale tier entries for ~5 minutes only. the 08:06 window shows sustained high concurrency: peak concurrent active requests ~180 for ~40s. Standard tier token bucket: 60/min with short burst allowance ~75 tokens. they exceeded the bucket by ~3x.

nisha: if the customer can justify a business-critical import/demo we can provision temporary headroom (default up to 6 hours). for anything longer or a permanent uplift, we need sales to sign a committed capacity/upgrade.

ashu: customer replies: the spike was a manual ingestion/retrieval job for a demo tomorrow — they request a 6-hour temporary burst. quote: "we didn't realize how concurrent our script would be; please allow 6 hours so the import finishes before our demo."

nisha: approve 6h temporary increase. conditions: support must log the approval, set auto-revert, and advise customer to implement throttling and batching. sales will follow up to discuss committed capacity if they expect sustained traffic.

clare: applying temporary uplift now. ticket notes:
- approval id: BSTR-20260313-57
- applied temporary bucket +3x for org o-ccf9 from 2026-03-13T09:00Z to 2026-03-13T15:00Z
- scheduled auto-revert and emailed customer with mitigation steps and recommended concurrency limits

ashu: customer confirmed receipt and adjusted their script to 50 concurrent and started batching arrays; retries dropped significantly after the uplift.

max: outcome — root cause is customer-side concurrent fan-out; billing propagation not the cause. action items:
- add internal KB: "recommended default concurrency by tier" with numbers and example curl->sdk migration notes
- educate on batching + SDK retries in onboarding flows

support-bot: auto-revert scheduled at 2026-03-13T15:00Z. ticket will auto-close after customer confirmation.

clare: closing the thread after we archive logs to the ticketing system and mark the incident as "mitigated - customer adjusted workload".
